sample_data.method: P08_school_results_public.json (the organisers' 25 published cases, 1,765 students) is loaded at start-up, one dataset per case. A 60-student demo dataset in the same format is also generated at start-up from a fixed seed (data.py, seed=42). Further cases or students can be uploaded as JSON on /upload.
sample_data.reset_instructions: Restart the Flask process. Everything is held in memory and rebuilt identically on start-up; there is no database or persisted state to clear.

problem_solving_method: A pure, Flask-free rules engine (grading.py) grades one subject at a time and returns the mark, the grade point and the published rule (R-10/R-11/R-12/R-13/R-29) that decided it, so the trace, the GPA and the checking-list membership all come from one code path. Data uses the organisers' case format throughout (6 compulsory subjects with Physics/Chemistry/Biology practicals, one optional subject per student from HMT/AGR/REL); datasets.py holds one dataset per case and upload.py validates JSON in that format with every rejection reason. app.py serves a searchable, sortable ledger whose student marksheet opens in a side panel, the office checklist, uploads, edits, a printable marksheet and a JSON export. tests/test_app.py checks every demo and published-case student against an independent implementation of the rules.

R1.evidence: data.py: build_demo_students() — 60 students, 30 in Class 9 and 30 in Class 10; six compulsory subjects (BAN, ENG, MAT, PHY, CHE, BIO) plus one optional per student (HMT, AGR or REL); PHY/CHE/BIO/HMT/AGR carry separate theory and practical marks. 11 hand-built edge cases (S001–S011): compulsory fail with a strong average, practical fail with passing theory, optional at 2.0, absent in a compulsory subject, absent in the optional only, theory fail with a strong practical, GPA cap, exact A- boundary, failed optional, a mark of 0 versus AB, optional lifting A- to A.

R2.evidence: grading.py: evaluate_subject() and evaluate_student() — grade point per subject, GPA via R-13 (capped at 5.00, 2dp, ROUND_HALF_UP), letter via R-10. Shown in the ledger and every marksheet; exported by /d/<dataset>/results.json. Verified against an independent implementation for all 1,765 published-case students (tests/test_app.py).

R3.evidence: templates/_marksheet.html — every subject shows the real theory/practical/combined or single mark, the grade point, the deciding rule and a note computed from that student's numbers. A compulsory failure names the failing subject(s) with their marks and keeps the uncancelled average visible (see S001).

R4.evidence: /d/<dataset>/checklist (app.py, templates/checklists.html) — the three R-29 lists (optional ≤ 2.0 including absent optional, practical below 8 in any subject, AB in any subject), each with a per-student reason quoting the marks; built from the same StudentResult as the GPA. The ledger can also be filtered to each list.

team_members.major_contribution: Grading engine, Flask routes, templates, the synthetic dataset with its 11 edge-case students, the upload format and validation, README and evaluation-manifest.json.

major_design_decisions: Adopted the organisers' case format as the only data model, so the demo, uploaded cases and the published file all go through one Dataset -> evaluate_student path.
One dataset per case, because student ids repeat between published cases; each keeps its own ledger and checklist.
The importer reports every reason a record is rejected, and one bad record never blocks the rest; the edit form goes through the same validator.
'AB' must be explicit: a blank value is rejected rather than treated as absent or 0, and AB is graded and labelled differently from a mark of 0.
GPA is rounded with Decimal + ROUND_HALF_UP so boundary GPAs land on the right letter grade.
The uncancelled average required by R-13 is computed for every student by the same code path as the published GPA.
The ledger is progressive enhancement: the server renders search, filter, sort and the open marksheet panel from the URL, and static/app.js makes it instant without page loads.
known_limitations: Absence in only one part of a practical subject is treated as absence for the whole subject (R-12 does not split theory/practical); the published cases only use whole-subject AB.
No persistence: uploads and edits live in memory and are lost on restart.
No authentication on upload or edit.
app.secret_key falls back to a development placeholder when SECRET_KEY is not set; it is only used for flash messages.

ai_tools_used.used_for: Helped write the grading engine, routes, templates, dataset, JSON importer and the ledger's search/sort/side-panel UI.
ai_tools_used.how_output_was_verified: tests/test_app.py compares every demo student and all 1,765 published-case students against an independent implementation of R-10–R-13 and R-29, checks each edge case, every importer rejection reason and every route; the running app was also driven in a browser (search, sort, panel, keyboard navigation, narrow screens).
